summary: Daya Krishna (1924–2007) worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as professor of philosophy and Ex-Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (circa 1969–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

Daya Ram Sahni (1879–1939) was an archaeologist and Indologist. After completing an M.A. at Oriental College and a doctorate at the University of the Punjab by 1903, he held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, Lucknow State Museum, and Jaipur State.

Dayananda Saraswati (1824–1883) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sri Jayachamarajendra Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and under Virajanand Dandeesha, P. S. Subramania Iyer, Veeraraghavachariar, Swami Pranavananda, Swami Tarananda Giri, and Swami Tapovan Maharaj.

Dayong (1893–1929) was an expert in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute, later teaching there in 1923. He also studied under Taixu, Paldan Tenzin Nyandrak, Bai Puren, and Dorje Geshe.

Debala Mitra (1925–2003) was a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983, succeeding Bal Krishen Thapar.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak (born 1931) is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cornell University (circa 1959–1961). He founded and served as director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages (circa 1969–1989) and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) was a philosopher and Indologist. He earned his B.A. at the University of Calcutta, studying under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta, and later served as a philosophy teacher at City College, Kolkata, and visiting professor at Calcutta.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD at Harvard under Oleg Grabar and a Habilitation at Vienna, she held professorships at UCLA and the University of Vienna (1994–2015).
Declan Quigley is a scholar in Indology and other fields. He has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei (born 1968) specializes in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. from Renmin University of China (circa 1995–1998) and became an associate professor of religious studies there around 2002.
Demchok Dorje studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Denis Sinor (1916–2011) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at Cambridge, subsequently teaching at Cambridge (1948–1962) and directing at Indiana University Bloomington (1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett (1925–2006) was a sinologist and historian who studied at SOAS and St Catharine's College. He held the Chair of Chinese at the University of London and the University of Cambridge before joining Princeton University (1980–1994).

Denise Bernot (1922–2016) was a scholar in linguistics. She studied at the École des chartes and École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and later held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from circa 1960 to 1989.

Denma Lochö Rinpoche (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. After studying at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric College under various masters, he served at the University of Calcutta, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and as Abbot of Namgyal Monastery.

Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012) and was affiliated with its South Asian, Tibetan and Buddhist Studies Library.

Dennis Genpo Merzel (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Southern California and its Rossier School of Education, and trained under Taizan Maezumi from circa 1972 to 1995.

Dennis Hirota (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. Educated at UC Berkeley and Nagoya University, he held posts at Hongwanji International Center, Chikushi Jogakuen University, Ryukoku University, and Harvard University.

Denzaburo Yoshizawa (1924–2003) was a philosopher who studied under Tetsuro Watsuji at the University of Tokyo (circa 1947–1950). He later held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (circa 1965–1987) and Iryo Sosei University (circa 1987–1999).

Derek F. Maher is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has taught at Virginia, UNC Greensboro, and East Carolina University.
